mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances despite a sustained FEDFUNDS decline, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate above 4.25% triggers a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 70% of triggered instances, or walk-forward Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 20,000 jobs signals labor market strength and consumer confidence, which elevates equity risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day forward returns in > 50% of instances despite rising PAYEMS, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting central banks to hold rates steady and reducing discount rates, which increases expected equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.
